cues: Titrations are named after the reaction they use.
Precipitation titrations, like silver nitrate against chloride, form an insoluble salt.
Complexometric titrations use E D T A.
And iodometric titrations use iodine and thiosulphate, with starch as the indicator.
Our syllabus focuses on the first two.
text: Titrations are named after the reaction they use. Acid base titrations use neutralisation. Redox titrations use electron transfer. Precipitation titrations, like silver nitrate against chloride, form an insoluble salt. Complexometric titrations use E D T A. And iodometric titrations use iodine and thiosulphate, with starch as the indicator. Our syllabus focuses on the first two.
